title: Contextualized Attention with Dynamic Kernel Selection
abstract: This paper introduces a novel attention mechanism designed to address the limitations of standard attention mechanisms, particularly their computational expense and potential inability to capture highly relevant relationships within sequences. The proposed approach, termed "Contextualized Attention with Dynamic Kernel Selection," dynamically adjusts the kernel function used to compute attention weights based on the surrounding contextual information. This adaptation is achieved through a small, trainable neural network that learns to select the most appropriate kernel for each query-key pair. The core idea is to move beyond fixed kernels, allowing the model to tailor its attention process to the specific characteristics of the input sequence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a framework for implementation. This work contributes to more efficient and accurate sequence modeling by mitigating the drawbacks of static attention.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize the field of topological analysis. Traditional topological analysis relies heavily on classical computational methods, often struggling with complex systems and computationally intensive tasks. We propose a novel framework leveraging quantum entanglement and transformations to simulate intricate topological phenomena with significantly enhanced speed and precision. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum states to represent and manipulate topological structures, offering a fundamentally different approach to analysis. This research investigates the feasibility of this framework and outlines its potential impact across various topological areas. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Багатокритеріальний вибір альтернатив кластеризації текстових даних за Silhouette та bootstrap-стабільністю
abstract: АНОТАЦІЯУ роботі досліджено проблему вибору альтернатив кластеризації текстових даних за умов, коли оцінювання результату лише за одним внутрішнім критерієм не дає повного уявлення про властивості сформованого розбиття.Значення Silhouette характеризує компактність і відокремленість кластерів, однак не відображає відтворюваність отриманого рішення за зміни складу вибірки.У зв'язку з цим метою дослідження є розроблення та експериментальна перевірка процедури багатокритеріального вибору альтернатив кластеризації текстових даних на основі спільного врахування Silhouette та bootstrap-стабільності.Стабільність визначається за допомогою повторних bootstrap-вибірок і порівняння сформованих розбиттів із базовим результатом за Adjusted Rand Index.Для узгодження двох критеріїв використано Pareto-аналіз, що дає змогу виділити множину компромісних альтернатив без введення довільних вагових коефіцієнтів.Експериментальну перевірку виконано на тематичному корпусі, сформованому на основі відкритого набору новинних текстів British Broadcasting Corporation, із використанням алгоритмів KMeans та агломеративної кластеризації Ward.Встановлено, що Silhouette та bootstrap-стабільність формують різні ранжування кластерних альтернатив.Для KMeans найбільше значення Silhouette отримано за десяти кластерів, тоді як максимальна bootstrap-стабільність спостерігалася за п'яти кластерів.Для Ward конфігурації з максимальними значеннями Silhouette, стабільності та зовнішньої якості також не збігалися.Це показує, що bootstrap-стабільність не може розглядатися як універсальний критерій правильності кластеризації, але надає додаткову інформацію про відтворюваність кластерного рішення.Застосування Pareto-домінування за Silhouette та bootstrapстабільністю дало змогу скоротити початкову множину з вісімнадцяти альтернатив до трьох недомінованих конфігурацій, тобто більш ніж на вісімдесят три відсотки.Еталонні тематичні мітки не використовувалися під час формування Paretoмножини та не входили до критеріїв багатокритеріального відбору; вони застосовувалися лише для зовнішнього оцінювання отриманих конфігурацій.Отримані результати підтверджують доцільність спільного аналізу внутрішньої геометричної якості та відтворюваності під час вибору альтернатив кластеризації текстових даних.

title: Multiple Myeloma Lesion Segmentation on Whole-Body Diffusion-Weighted Imaging via Efficient Anatomical Anticipation and Multimodal Confirmation
abstract: Whole-body diffusion-weighted imaging (WB-DWI) is widely used for multiple myeloma (MM) assessment, yet automated lesion segmentation remains challenging due to limited anatomical delineation and the low specificity of marrow hyperintensity. Existing studies have introduced bone region-of-interest (ROI) information and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps to mitigate these ambiguities, but practical limitations remain. Bone ROI construction often relies on costly manual annotation, image registration, or dedicated bone models, while ADC is usually incorporated only through simple channel fusion, limiting its ability to provide complementary structural and lesion-discriminative cues. To address these limitations, we propose a two-stage framework for MM lesion segmentation on WB-DWI. In the first stage, we train a bone ROI generation model from ADC images without dedicated bone labels, providing an efficient and practical anatomical prior for lesion analysis. In the second stage, we propose Anatomy-guided Multimodal U-Net (AMU-Net), which leverages ADC in a manner consistent with clinical lesion assessment rather than treating it as a generic auxiliary modality. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method. It achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated methods, with a mean Dice score of 76.2%.

title: FEDERATED LEARNING-BASED PRIVACY PRESERVATION FOR INTELLIGENT DATA ANALYTICS
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a new machine learning paradigm that allows different users and organizations to jointly learn an intelligent model without sharing local private data. Federated learning retains data locally on devices and sends only model updates to a central server to prevent the owners from losing their data. It can dramatically curtail confidential risks to sensitive information across a variety of sectors, including healthcare, finance, smart cities, and Internet of Things (IoT) use. In this paper, the authors discuss the potential of federated learning in intelligent data analytics with privacy. Briefly introduces the key concepts, current research, privacy concerns, communications issues, and security solutions for a federated environment. The results reported the potential advantages of federated learning in the context of secure and intelligent data analysis, while preserving data privacy. Keywords: Federated Learning, Data Privacy, Intelligent Data Analytics, Machine Learning, Data Security, Privacy Preservation

title: Vector Database Dataset
abstract: Dataset generated from the following paper. AbstractBackground Strict privacy regulations and institutional barriers have created persistent medical data silos, limiting the development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) models across healthcare institutions. Although federated learning provides a potential solution, it still requires access to decentralized patient-level data and faces challenges related to interoperability, computational complexity, and institutional governance. We investigated whether a private-domain clinical vector database could enhance deep learning-based outcome prediction without exchanging raw patient data. Methods We retrospectively collected 10 years of real-world electronic health records (EHRs) from more than 40,000 cardiovascular inpatients at a tertiary hospital in Shanghai, China. The clinical cohort included patients hospitalized with cardiovascular diseases, with outcomes defined as in-hospital mortality and readmission events. Clinical text records were transformed into high-dimensional representations using a locally constructed Word2Vec-based cardiovascular clinical vector database. We developed and compared two modeling pipelines: (1) conventional pretrained language models using clinical text representations alone, and (2) hybrid models integrating pretrained language models with private-domain vector embeddings through embedding fusion. 20% of patients were independently reserved as a test cohort. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, calibration performance, and prediction variance. Results Pretrained language models, including ChineseBERT, RoBERTa, and MacBERT, achieved reliable baseline performance for cardiovascular outcome prediction. Incorporation of the private clinical vector database significantly improved predictive performance, with ChineseBERT- and MacBERT-based hybrid models achieving approximately 10% absolute increases in AUC, while RoBERTa demonstrated a consistent improvement of approximately 2% in AUC. The vector-enhanced models also showed improved calibration and reduced prediction variability compared with standalone language models. Conclusions This study establishes a private-domain cardiovascular clinical vector database constructed from long-term real-world EHRs and demonstrates that model–model interaction through local embedding integration can improve deep learning prediction of cardiovascular in-hospital mortality and readmission outcomes. By enabling knowledge enhancement without patient-level data sharing, this framework provides a scalable and privacy-preserving strategy to overcome healthcare data silos and facilitates the development of precision cardiovascular AI systems.

title: Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? – Verified Analysis Dataset
abstract: AI Cyber Paper: verified analysis and scientific audit This archive reproduces the available numerical calculations for Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? It preserves the supplied paper ZIP, curated original defensive artifacts and their cloud capture receipts. It also contains a source-linked scientific audit, the recovery inventory, analysis code and verification controls. It is not a complete experimental reproduction archive. It does not contain all original agent prompts, raw trajectories or executable attack outputs. Historical model calls, environment execution and grading are not rerun. The audit found missing delivered diagnostics and a sampled CLI version mismatch. Reproducing the recorded numbers does not establish the validity of those historical experimental conditions. Start here File What it answers dossier/SCIENTIFIC_REVIEW.md What was sampled, what was recovered, which objections survived, and what remains unknown dossier/REPRODUCTION_SCOPE.md Exactly which calculations and evidence checks can be repeated from this ZIP dossier/CLAIM_UPDATES.csv Current interpretations, with exact manuscript lines and evidence references numerical/PAPER_NUMBERS.csv The preserved 806-row historical register of paper numbers and source lines FILE_GUIDE.md How the directories, code and original artifacts fit together CONTENTS.csv One description and category for each deliverable file, except itself and the manifest MANIFEST.json Exact file membership, byte sizes, SHA-256 hashes and category totals The paper’s questions are paired direction (the defender-minus-attacker differential on identical instances) and system heterogeneity (how that differential changes across model/harness configurations). See the unchanged paper-v2.0.0/main.tex, lines 79–83, inside paper/original/Does_AI_Help_Cyber_Attackers_or_Defenders.zip. Reproduce offline Use Python 3.12. Keep the environment and outputs outside this extracted directory so that its exact membership stays intact. The -B flag prevents Python from adding bytecode caches to the sealed tree. python3.12 -m venv ../ai-cyber-analysis-env ../ai-cyber-analysis-env/bin/python -m pip install -r numerical/requirements.txt ../ai-cyber-analysis-env/bin/python -B verify.py ../ai-cyber-analysis-env/bin/python -B run.py --output ../ai-cyber-analysis-results Dependency installation may use the network. Verification and numerical analysis do not require credentials, cloud access, raw recovery archives, models, containers or environment images. The runner checks the pinned dependencies, all package hashes, original/receipt bindings and metadata consistency before copying the numerical component to the new output. It runs all 11 stages there and refuses to overwrite an existing output directory. The outer result is receipt.json; detailed tables, figures, stage logs and the numerical receipt are under numerical/results/reproduction/. Successful completion is explicitly VERIFIED_ANALYSIS_WITH_SCIENTIFIC_LIMITATIONS. The historical primary-stage label COMPLETE_NUMERICAL_REPRODUCTION refers only to that stage’s arithmetic. Verify the actual ZIP The adjacent .sha256 file and .verification.json record the release ZIP digest. An internal manifest alone cannot authenticate itself if both the files and manifest are changed. Supply the independently recorded ZIP digest: python3.12 -B verify.py --zip ../AI_Cyber_Paper_Verified_Analysis_2026-09-05.zip --expected-sha256 RELEASE_SHA256 ZIP verification checks exact membership, safe canonical paths, regular-file types, hashes and CRCs without extracting. Extracted-tree verification additionally checks the included originals and metadata relationships. It does not rehash omitted source bodies or certify model behavior. release_pin_checked reports whether an independent digest was actually supplied. Included quantities One unchanged supplied paper ZIP: 12 members, 101,154 bytes. 1,386 original defensive patches and 1,318 original evaluator inputs; 2,704 matching capture receipts. Five frozen numerical input files, covering 1,907 classified main observations, 1,992 February records, 276 health records, 1,660 health observations and 424 diagnostic fingerprints. These populations overlap. Nine locked audit trials: three main attacker/defender pairs and three February trials. A 1,992-row input reconciliation and exact references for 3,030 original bodies checked during its derivation. 877 export-object metadata candidates from 134 original provider response pages; 183 match primary defender jobs. Candidate object bodies are absent. One separately inspected export has a measured metadata projection. The original statistical source, the runnable analytical derivative, build/verification code and actual validation receipts. The original paper contains two manuscripts, three bibliography files, two identical figure copies, two changelogs, one Overleaf README and two talk files. Some are unnecessary for arithmetic but remain because the supplied source ZIP is preserved intact. The small numerical/paper/source.zip is an intentional three-member subset needed by the existing numerical consumers. Development and rebuilding ../ai-cyber-analysis-env/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt ../ai-cyber-analysis-env/bin/python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests ../ai-cyber-analysis-env/bin/python -B package.py --output ../another-analysis-release.zip Rebuilding deliberately creates a new manifest and external digest; it cannot preserve a prior release’s identity after edits. Do not confuse a newly resealed archive with an independently authenticated historical release. Recovery commands and required external inputs are documented in dossier/REPRODUCTION_SCOPE.md. No experimental observation, prompt, trajectory, patch or cloud log was synthesized to close a gap. New code, tables, reports and validation outputs are clearly identified as derived analysis or development evidence.

title: Graph Transformers with Attention-Based Relational Reasoning
abstract: Graph Transformers have demonstrated impressive performance in various graph-related tasks. However, their standard attention mechanism often struggles to effectively capture complex relational dependencies within graphs. This paper proposes an enhanced Graph Transformer architecture that integrates attention-based relational reasoning. We modify the standard Graph Transformer's attention mechanism to enable nodes to attend to all nodes in the graph, with the attention weights determined by a learned relational similarity score. This allows the model to explicitly model and leverage the relationships between nodes, leading to improved performance on graph-based learning tasks. The core contribution lies in broadening the scope of attention within Graph Transformers, facilitating the capture of richer relational dependencies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and a comprehensive evaluation on benchmark graph datasets.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Graph Representations via Contrastive Predictive Coding
abstract: Self-supervised learning has emerged as a powerful technique for learning representations from unlabeled data, particularly in domains like computer vision and natural language processing. However, its application to graph data has been limited, primarily due to the lack of effective inductive biases that can guide the learning process and effectively capture the intricate structural relationships inherent in graphs. This paper proposes a novel self-supervised learning framework for graph representation learning based on contrastive predictive coding (CPC). The core idea is to train nodes to predict their future states based on their past states and the states of their neighbors, thereby learning graph representations through a predictive process. This approach introduces a strong inductive bias related to graph connectivity and relationships, leading to improved graph representation quality. We formulate the learning process as a contrastive prediction task, where nodes are encouraged to accurately predict their future states while distinguishing them from inaccurate predictions generated by noisy or unrelated data. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and inherent design principles.

title: Quantum State Multi-Modal Correlation Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the intricate correlations within multi-modal quantum states, presenting a novel theoretical framework and analytical methodology. The core of the research lies in applying quantum information theory and statistical physics to model and understand the complex behaviors inherent in multi-modal quantum systems. We aim to move beyond traditional approaches by establishing a robust mathematical framework for quantifying and characterizing multi-modal entanglement and correlations, specifically focusing on scenarios where multiple quantum systems are linked. The developed methods offer a new perspective on manipulating and controlling these systems, with potential implications for quantum computation, quantum communication, and fundamental quantum information theory. The key contributions include a generalized correlation function, a multi-modal entanglement measure, and an approach to analyzing the dynamics of multi-modal quantum systems. The work explores the connections between classical statistical mechanics and quantum entanglement in these systems, providing insights into the emergence of correlations at the quantum level. ---

title: Core Claim: Researching dynamic information encoding based on geometric topology, aiming to enhance quantum data transmission in quantum computing and quantum communication through the utilization of quantum entanglement and geometric properties.
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum data transmission leveraging geometric topology. Quantum data encoding, traditionally focused on classical data, is reimagined to utilize the unique properties of geometric topology to create robust and efficient quantum communication channels. The core mechanism centers on encoding data as quantum states, and exploiting the inherent correlations of quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced security and increased data transfer rates. This work investigates the potential of geometric topology to revolutionize quantum communication, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to existing techniques. We demonstrate the feasibility of encoding complex data structures using geometric topology, specifically focusing on minimizing the number of qubits required for transmission and maximizing the fidelity of the encoded data. The study explores various geometric topologies and their corresponding impact on the security and efficiency of quantum data transfer, ultimately proposing a robust framework for dynamic information encoding within quantum systems. The research utilizes a combination of theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to validate the proposed methodology, highlighting its potential for significant advancements in quantum communication. The analysis considers various geometric topologies, including hyperbolic geometry and projective geometry, and their implications for data security and transmission rates. We present preliminary results demonstrating improved data security and enhanced transmission rates compared to existing methods, showcasing the practical viability of this geometric topology-based approach. Further research will focus on refining the encoding process and exploring the application of this technique to more complex data types.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Theory Simulations
abstract: Quantum-enhanced chaos theory simulations represent a paradigm shift in computational modeling, offering the potential for dramatically accelerated and improved simulations of complex, chaotic systems. This paper explores the integration of quantum entanglement and superposition into a novel computational framework designed to overcome the limitations of classical methods. We detail the core mechanism of utilizing quantum states to represent critical variables and enhance the representation of chaotic dynamics, highlighting the potential for exponential speedups and unprecedented detail in the simulation of chaotic phenomena. The research focuses on the creation of a hybrid quantum-classical simulation approach, emphasizing the strategic application of quantum mechanics to enhance the fidelity of chaotic system dynamics. This work aims to establish a foundation for future advancements in chaotic system modeling, driven by the unique capabilities of quantum computation.

title: Quantum Topological Dimension
abstract: Quantum Topological Dimension (QTD) proposes a novel approach to quantum computation and information storage by linking the concept of quantum state dimensionality to topological quantum geometry. This framework envisions quantum states as inherently possessing topological properties, allowing for the implementation of revolutionary quantum algorithms and data storage paradigms. This paper introduces the core concept of "Quantum Topological Dimension," outlines a foundational quantum computing architecture predicated on this principle, and discusses the potential benefits and challenges associated with this paradigm shift. We explore the theoretical foundations and potential applications of QTD, emphasizing its unique capabilities compared to conventional quantum computing.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning Feature Matching Mechanism
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive machine learning framework for dynamic feature matching, aiming to enhance model performance through a novel mechanism. Traditional feature matching methods often struggle with data drift and lack the adaptability of modern machine learning models. Our proposed framework leverages the self-adaptive nature of deep learning models to dynamically adjust feature matching parameters, offering a more flexible and robust approach. We detail the core mechanism, its advantages, and potential applications. This work addresses the limitations of static feature matching by integrating a dynamically adaptive parameter tuning process.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应矩阵运算
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to matrix computation leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. We propose a self-adaptive matrix multiplication algorithm that utilizes quantum entanglement to optimize the computational process, resulting in significant improvements in efficiency compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around establishing entangled states between matrix elements, allowing for instantaneous correlations to guide the computation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through rigorous analysis and simulation, highlighting its potential to revolutionize matrix operations. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Generation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense promise for revolutionary advancements in computation and information processing. However, harnessing its full potential is hampered by the challenges of maintaining and manipulating entangled states. This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum entanglement generation algorithm designed to address these challenges by intelligently constructing entanglement structures, optimizing for efficiency and robustness. We propose a mechanism that leverages the inherent self-adaptive nature of quantum entanglement to autonomously generate more effective entanglement configurations, ultimately enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms. This paper details the core concepts, the proposed algorithm's architecture, and preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in generating enhanced entanglement. The focus is on improving the scalability and efficiency of quantum computations, moving beyond static entanglement generation approaches.

title: 自适应几何拓扑的量子信息熵计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for quantum information entropy calculation based on adaptive geometric topology. The core idea is to leverage the inherent self-correlation of quantum states to precisely determine entropy. We propose a quantum state transformation scheme that dynamically adjusts the geometric topology of the quantum system, achieving a higher degree of accuracy and robustness compared to traditional entropy calculation methods. The algorithm's effectiveness is validated through simulations and preliminary experimental results demonstrating improved entropy estimation. The research focuses on enhancing quantum information security through precise and efficient entropy estimation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Analysis and Accelerated Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate no matter how far apart they are, has long captured the imagination of physicists and engineers alike. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize computation, particularly through the development of a novel acceleration algorithm predicated on the principles of non-locality. We investigate the impact of entanglement on information transfer and computational capabilities, proposing a new algorithm architecture leveraging entanglement for enhanced speed and efficiency. This work aims to demonstrate the feasibility of harnessing quantum entanglement to overcome limitations inherent in classical computing paradigms. The core claim is that a framework for analyzing quantum entanglement and a corresponding acceleration algorithm can significantly impact the performance of computationally challenging tasks. The study will analyze the strengths and weaknesses of existing approaches to quantum computation, specifically focusing on the application of entanglement to accelerate algorithmic operations. The research will also consider the challenges and potential advancements in this field.

title: Meta-Learning for Algorithm Transfer Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of meta-learning techniques to algorithm transfer learning, addressing the challenge of efficiently adapting algorithms to new domains. Traditional transfer learning often relies on manually designed adaptation strategies, which can be domain-specific and require substantial effort. We propose a meta-learning framework where a meta-learner learns to quickly adapt algorithms by analyzing task and environmental characteristics. The core claim is that by learning *how* to transfer, the meta-learner significantly improves algorithmic generalization. The mechanism involves training the meta-learner to adjust algorithm parameters and structures based on observed task features. This approach offers a more automated and potentially more effective solution compared to conventional transfer learning methods. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline a potential implementation strategy. The key contribution lies in the automated learning of adaptation strategies, leading to improved performance across diverse domains. ---

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Topography Protocol
abstract: This paper introduces a novel protocol, the Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Topography Protocol (DETP), designed to establish and maintain robust and scalable quantum entanglement within a topological network. The core innovation lies in the utilization of adaptive optimization algorithms, specifically reinforcement learning, to dynamically adjust entanglement parameters between nodes in the network. This approach overcomes the inherent limitations of static and fragile entanglement commonly found in traditional quantum networks. The protocol leverages the non-commutative nature of entanglement within a topological network, coupled with real-time feedback from the receiver, to maximize entanglement fidelity and extend transmission distances. The DETP offers a significant advancement in quantum communication, paving the way for more resilient and scalable quantum information transfer. Mathematical models and algorithms are presented, detailing the control mechanisms and performance metrics of the proposed protocol. The protocol's key elements include a dynamically adjusted entanglement map, a reinforcement learning agent optimizing the entanglement parameters, and a feedback loop ensuring robust entanglement maintenance. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the protocol's ability to mitigate the effects of noise and channel imperfections, ultimately leading to enhanced quantum communication performance.

title: Quantum State Tomography with Measurement Device Independent Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum state tomography (QST) is a critical technique for characterizing the state of quantum systems, particularly in the context of quantum computing. Traditional QST protocols rely heavily on precise knowledge of the measurement devices used, introducing significant vulnerabilities to systematic errors and device imperfections. This paper proposes a novel measurement device-independent (MDI) quantum state tomography protocol designed specifically for multi-qubit systems. The core principle of this approach is the strategic utilization of entanglement to minimize the impact of device-specific biases, thereby achieving a more robust and accurate reconstruction of the quantum state. The protocol involves a carefully designed series of measurements performed by multiple, potentially imperfect, measurement devices. Through analyzing the correlations generated by these measurements, we can, with a high degree of certainty, deduce the underlying quantum state without requiring perfect knowledge of each individual device. This MDI QST method represents a significant advancement in overcoming the limitations of conventional QST, paving the way for more reliable and scalable quantum state characterization in complex quantum computing architectures. The theoretical framework and key equations are presented, demonstrating the feasibility and advantages of this approach.

title: All for 1-Bit: Towards Genuine 1-Bit Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress, yet their massive storage and memory-bandwidth demands still hinder efficient deployment. Weight binarization is a promising solution, but existing binarization-based post-training quantization (PTQ) methods usually far exceed the nominal 1-bit storage target due to hidden overhead. To address this gap, we propose All for 1-Bit (AF1), a genuine 1-bit PTQ framework for LLMs. AF1 comprises two complementary components: (1) Null-space-Aware Binary Factorization (NABF) for improving binary reconstruction through Hessian-aware surrogate reparameterization, null-space-aware binary factorization, and scale-only global reconstruction; and (2) Hierarchical Shapley Allocation (HiSA) for assigning structural capacity using hierarchical Shapley sensitivity. Together, they preserve model accuracy under a strict 1.0-BPW budget in the PTQ setting. Experiments on LLaMA, Qwen, and Gemma families show that AF1 consistently outperforms existing binarization-based PTQ methods in perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Compared with BF16, AF1 achieves an average 2.5 times inference speedup and over 90% memory reduction across evaluated models, providing a practical path toward deployable genuine 1-bit compression for LLMs. The code for reproducibility is available at https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/AF1.

title: PAI-Actor: Cinematic Multi-Character Replacement in Dynamic Scenes
abstract: We present PAI-Actor, a cinematic multi-character animation framework for character replacement in dynamic movie scenes. Unlike conventional animation systems that mainly drive a single static image or a single subject, our goal is to replace and animate multiple characters within real video clips while preserving the original scene dynamics, camera motion, and background content. This setting is particularly challenging because the generated characters must remain consistent with the source performance in motion and interaction, while also matching the surrounding background in lighting, shadow, composition, and overall cinematic appearance. To address this, we formulate multi-character animation as a structure-guided human recovery problem and build a movie-driven training pipeline from high-quality film data. Furthermore, to support practical cinematic production, we introduce a bidirectional-to-autoregressive distillation framework: we first train a bidirectional diffusion transformer for high-quality short-clip generation at 1080P resolution, and then distill it into an autoregressive video-to-video model for efficient inference and longer video generation. Experiments show that PAI-Actor enables high-fidelity multi-character animation with strong scene consistency, cinematic visual quality, and efficient long-form generation.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Parallel Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithm optimization leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea centers on utilizing entangled qubits to facilitate instantaneous data transfer and correlated operations between distinct quantum processors, effectively bypassing the limitations imposed by the speed of light in classical communication. This paradigm shift allows for a true parallel computation model, significantly enhancing algorithmic efficiency, particularly for computationally intensive tasks. We outline a framework for designing such algorithms, detailing the key considerations for establishing and maintaining entanglement, and exploring potential applications. The fundamental difference from conventional parallel computing lies in the direct exploitation of quantum mechanics, rather than relying on hardware-centric parallel architectures. The theoretical underpinnings are presented, focusing on the mathematical formulation of entanglement-based operations and their impact on computational speed. The proposed methodology offers a pathway towards dramatically accelerating algorithms across a range of disciplines, including machine learning, optimization, and simulations.

title: Quantum Variational Transform for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper explores the application of Quantum Variational Transform (QVT) to solve optimization problems. QVT leverages the principles of quantum invisibility and transformation to convert complex optimization challenges into solvable quantum problems. The core mechanism involves mapping the original problem onto a quantum system and utilizing quantum computation to identify the optimal solution. This approach expands the applicability of variational methods to the quantum realm, offering a potentially efficient quantum optimization algorithm. This work details the theoretical framework and outlines the methodology for implementing QVT, demonstrating its potential impact on a range of optimization problems. The key contribution lies in providing a novel strategy for tackling difficult optimization tasks using the unique capabilities of quantum computation.

title: Quantum Neural Networks with Bio-Inspired Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for quantum neural networks (QNNs) inspired by biological neural networks, specifically focusing on adaptive learning capabilities. The core idea is to integrate biological mechanisms such as synaptic plasticity and long-range dependencies into the quantum learning process. The traditional approach to QNN training often relies on gradient-based methods, which can be inefficient and susceptible to local minima. This work introduces a bio-inspired approach that leverages the inherent parallelism and quantum superposition of QNNs to achieve more robust and adaptive learning. We formulate the learning process using a modified Hebbian learning rule combined with a quantum measurement process. The key innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the quantum gates based on the network's internal state, mimicking the neural network's ability to adapt to changing environments. The resulting QNN architecture exhibits enhanced learning speed and improved generalization performance compared to conventional QNNs. The theoretical framework is presented, and the underlying mathematical equations are detailed, providing a robust foundation for further research and development in this field.

title: Multi-Modal Knowledge Graph Construction via Self-Training
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge graph construction leveraging multi-modal data and self-training. title: Symbolic Regression with Grammatical Evolution for Discovering Mathematical Laws
abstract: This paper investigates the application of grammatical evolution (GE) combined with symbolic regression (SR) for the automated discovery of mathematical laws from datasets. The core challenge in this field lies in the ability to effectively navigate the exponentially large search space of possible mathematical expressions. Traditional GE often faces difficulties when dealing with complex systems, leading to limitations in the complexity of the discovered laws. We propose an enhanced approach that leverages the strengths of both GE and SR, creating a more robust and powerful system for mathematical law discovery. Specifically, we integrate GE's evolutionary adaptation with SR's symbolic manipulation capabilities, resulting in a search space that allows for the generation of significantly more complex and accurate mathematical models. The paper presents a detailed methodology and theoretical framework for this combined approach, and highlights its potential for tackling challenging problems in diverse scientific domains. Experimental results, while not involving formal experiments, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in discovering mathematical relationships from synthetic datasets, showcasing its ability to identify intricate patterns and generate sophisticated mathematical equations.

title: Quantum Decoherence Control for Complex System Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum decoherence control to optimize complex systems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and dynamic nature of systems such as supply chains and transportation networks. We propose a novel approach leveraging the principles of quantum decoherence. Specifically, we introduce the concept of "decoherence interventions," strategically applied during system operation to manipulate parameters and mitigate negative impacts, ultimately leading to dynamic optimization. The core idea is to exploit the controllable nature of decoherence – a fundamental quantum phenomenon – to achieve a level of precision not attainable with classical methods. This work lays the groundwork for a new paradigm in optimization, potentially unlocking significant improvements in system performance and resilience. The theoretical framework presented provides a foundation for future research exploring the practical implementation and scalability of this technique. We present a mathematical model demonstrating the core principles and illustrate the potential for adaptive control strategies.

title: Dynamic Programming for Quantum State Tomography with Entangled Photon Sources
abstract: Quantum state tomography (QST) is a fundamental procedure in quantum information science, enabling the precise characterization of quantum states. Traditional QST methods often require a prohibitive number of measurements, particularly for complex quantum states, significantly limiting their practical application. This work presents a novel approach to QST leveraging dynamic programming. The core idea is to iteratively refine a quantum state estimate based on measurement data, minimizing the total number of measurements needed to achieve a desired level of accuracy. The algorithm constructs a dynamic programming table, storing partial state estimates and their associated probabilities, allowing for efficient exploration of the state space. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential advantages over conventional methods. The key contribution lies in the algorithm's ability to adaptively adjust the measurement strategy, focusing on regions of the state space with the highest uncertainty, leading to a substantial reduction in measurement requirements. The performance of the algorithm is discussed in terms of computational complexity and accuracy achieved.

title: Non-Euclidean Vector Spaces for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing non-Euclidean vector spaces to enhance the representation and generalization capabilities of machine learning models. Traditional Euclidean space, while widely used, often struggles with high-dimensional data and the inherent complexities of real-world datasets. This research proposes a novel framework centered around defining and manipulating metric spaces that explicitly capture non-linear relationships, allowing for more robust and adaptable models. We introduce a 'metric' that quantifies the similarity between data points, enabling the model to better isolate and represent underlying patterns. The core mechanism involves a mathematical transformation that maps data points onto this metric space, mitigating the limitations of traditional vector spaces. This approach promises to improve model performance, particularly in scenarios involving noise and complex data structures. The paper details the mathematical foundations of this metric, its implementation within a machine learning context, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: 拓扑-量子融合算法的优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed "拓扑-量子融合算法", designed to address complex system parameter configuration optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on classical computation, while this approach integrates topological and quantum entanglement to enhance computational efficiency. The algorithm leverages quantum entanglement to accelerate the optimization process, leading to improved parameter configuration. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness in solving specific optimization problems. The core mechanism centers around constructing a topological structure that guides the exploration of parameter space and utilizing entanglement to accelerate the search for optimal configurations. This paper explores the potential of this integrated approach to enhance optimization performance, particularly for systems with intricate parameter landscapes.

title: Dynamic Semantic Weaving Network (DSN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Weaving Network (DSN), a novel approach to understanding and predicting the behavior of complex systems. DSN leverages a distributed, evolutionary algorithm-based "semantic weaver" to dynamically extract, validate, and construct high-level semantic abstractions from underlying hardware, software, and user interaction data. The core claim is that this dynamic process enables adaptive understanding and prediction of system behavior in real-time. The system employs a network topology where nodes represent diverse data sources, and the semantic weaver, driven by a genetic algorithm and reinforcement learning, iteratively evaluates data source semantic consistency and automatically builds and updates a semantic graph. This graph incorporates static information alongside probabilistic models and predictive capabilities for data source behavior. Nodes collaborate by sharing and validating the semantic graph. DSN distinguishes itself from existing static semantic modeling techniques through its adaptive, distributed nature, enabling real-time adaptation to system changes and uncertainties. The combination of evolutionary algorithms and reinforcement learning facilitates automatic semantic consistency validation and adaptive graph optimization, a feature largely absent in current semantic modeling approaches.

title: Adaptive Quantum Geometry: Dynamic Topology Mapping and Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive quantum geometry to dynamic topology mapping and optimization. We introduce a novel method for generating and manipulating quantum states based on a dynamically evolving geometric structure. This approach utilizes a feedback loop that iteratively adjusts parameters to achieve complex calculations and optimize outcomes. The core concept lies in leveraging the inherent properties of quantum geometry – specifically, its sensitivity to initial conditions and its ability to exhibit complex, non-intuitive transformations – to guide the optimization process. The method's potential impact spans diverse fields, including materials science, quantum computing, and optimization algorithms, offering a paradigm shift in how we approach complex problems. This work presents a framework for dynamically shaping quantum states, enabling unprecedented levels of control and precision in computational and analytical tasks.

title: Quantum Error Correction Networks via Complementary Information Encoding
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum error correction within a network architecture, termed complementary information encoding. The core claim is that by utilizing complementary encoding strategies leveraging quantum entanglement, it's possible to achieve non-local error correction, moving beyond the limitations of purely local, neighboring-node correction schemes. The proposed mechanism involves designing an encoding protocol that distributes redundant information across the network via quantum entanglement, significantly expanding the coverage and efficiency of the error correction process. This approach fundamentally shifts from local reliance to global error detection, inherently increasing the network's overall error tolerance. We detail the mathematical framework and theoretical considerations underpinning this new strategy, focusing on the key parameters influencing its performance. The presented method offers a potentially more robust and scalable solution for quantum information transmission and storage compared to conventional local error correction techniques.

title: Information-Theoretic Grounding of Neural Language Models
abstract: Neural language models (NLMs) have achieved remarkable success in various natural language processing tasks, but they are often criticized for lacking genuine understanding. This paper proposes a novel approach to grounding NLMs by explicitly incorporating information-theoretic principles. We argue that current models operate primarily on statistical correlations within text data, failing to connect language to underlying physical concepts. Our core claim is that a fundamental limitation of existing NLMs is their absence of a connection to the real world. We introduce a training mechanism that maximizes mutual information between the model's representations and these underlying concepts, effectively forcing the model to learn a more physically informed representation of language. The proposed method utilizes Shannon entropy and mutual information calculations throughout the training process. We demonstrate, theoretically, how this approach can lead to a more robust and semantically richer language model. The key contribution lies in providing a mathematically rigorous framework for grounding language models, moving beyond purely statistical learning towards a conceptually driven representation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Model based on Bio-Information
abstract: This research investigates the potential of utilizing bio-information as a foundational element to construct a novel quantum entanglement model. Traditional quantum entanglement models often rely on complex mathematical frameworks, limiting their applicability to specific scenarios. This work proposes a paradigm shift by explicitly incorporating biological information – specifically, the structure of biochemical reactions and the inherent information encoded within biological data – into the model's core. We aim to simulate quantum entanglement's physical properties and evolution by dynamically modeling these biological elements. This integrated approach promises to offer a more intuitive and potentially more robust framework for understanding and potentially manipulating quantum phenomena. The core mechanism centers around creating a computational model that mirrors the intricate interplay of biological systems and quantum mechanics. The research explores the implications of such a model for various quantum computing applications and the potential for novel insights into the fundamental nature of entanglement.

title: Differential Privacy with Gradient Propagation for Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data, preserving data privacy. However, traditional differential privacy (DP) techniques, when directly applied to the gradient updates in FL, often lead to substantial communication overhead and a detrimental impact on model accuracy. This paper introduces a novel gradient propagation scheme that integrates differential privacy directly into the local training process of each client. Our method, termed Gradient Propagation with Differential Privacy (GP-DP), aims to minimize the information leakage while maintaining a high level of privacy protection. The core of our approach lies in carefully designing the propagation strategy to reduce the number of gradient updates transmitted to the central server. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and a simplified model, that GP-DP significantly reduces communication costs compared to standard DP-FL and provides a more accurate model compared to approaches relying solely on local DP. The key innovation is the adaptive adjustment of the propagation steps based on the client's local gradient magnitude, thereby balancing privacy and utility. This work represents a significant step towards practical and effective privacy-preserving federated learning systems.

title: Causal Representation Learning via Counterfactual Diffusion Networks
abstract: This paper introduces Counterfactual Diffusion Networks (CDN), a novel approach to causal representation learning. Traditional representation learning methods often fail to accurately capture underlying causal relationships within data, leading to issues in downstream tasks that rely on understanding these relationships. CDN addresses this limitation by employing a diffusion model to simulate counterfactual scenarios. The core idea is to learn representations that reflect how changes to one variable propagate through the system, effectively capturing causal dependencies. The diffusion process allows the network to learn robust representations even in the presence of noise and confounding variables. We demonstrate that CDN outperforms existing correlation-based methods in capturing causal structure and improves the accuracy of causal inference tasks. The key contributions of this work are the integration of diffusion models with counterfactual reasoning and the demonstration of CDN's effectiveness in learning causal representations.

title: From Splats to Silicon: Rethinking Computational Efficiency of 3DGS
abstract: 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) represents scenes with explicit primitives and supports real-time novel-view synthesis, yet its system efficiency varies substantially across scenes, viewpoints, rendering paths, and platform constraints. Existing studies pursue efficiency through representation and algorithm design, GPU runtime optimization, and architectural support, but their reported gains correspond to different points along the rendering and update paths. Connecting these indicators to end-to-end system benefit requires tracing how each optimization changes Gaussian selection, screen-space work, data movement, and stage or frame time. We therefore use a workload-centric framework to connect representation and algorithm research, GPU runtimes, and hardware architectures and to identify recurring workload patterns. We complement literature analysis with reproduced measurements and controlled GPU profiling of selected implementations, relating workload counts to stage time and memory traffic. Together, these comparisons show that system gains depend on workload reductions reaching downstream execution, granularity matching each stage, and the cost of data transfers, synchronization, and cached results, gradients, and optimizer data. Building on these findings, we discuss more consistent evaluation under rendering-quality constraints and identify key directions for future system design.

title: Quantum Message Passing Convergence and Vanishing Block-Error Probability for Random LDPC Codes
abstract: Belief propagation with quantum messages (BPQM) is a quantum algorithm that decodes classical codes transmitted over classical--quantum channels. It realizes optimal decoding on tree factor graphs over pure-state classical-quantum channels. However, this tree-based analysis does not ensure vanishing block-error probability for LDPC Tanner graphs with cycles. In this work, we construct a two-stage BPQM decoder for random $q$-ary LDPC codes over symmetric $q$-ary pure-state channels, where $q$ is prime, and prove that its ensemble-average block-error probability vanishes as the blocklength $N$ tends to infinity. For regular ensembles with $d_v\geq3$, fidelity bounds yield double-exponential decay of the average symbol-error probability throughout the BPQM success region. We apply depth-$\ell$ BPQM to coordinates with tree neighbourhoods and treat the remaining coordinates as erasures. With a suitable $\ell=Θ(\log\log N)$, a noncommutative union bound controls the BPQM decoding errors, while the minimum-distance property guarantees erasure recovery. We also extend the analysis to finite-support irregular ensembles. These results are relevant to quantum algorithms based on Regev's reduction, where coherent decoding uncomputes a codeword register. Decoded quantum interferometry (DQI) uses a closely related Fourier-based framework that reduces sparse max-LINSAT optimization problems to LDPC decoding problems on pure-state channels. Our results justify the use of BPQM in the decoding step of DQI and of coding-theoretic algorithms based on Regev's reduction whenever the code is drawn from one of the random LDPC ensembles analyzed here and the induced memoryless symmetric pure-state channel lies in the BPQM success region. Curiously, our numerical results indicate that DQI+BPQM achieves a satisfaction ratio that closely matches that of simulated annealing.

title: Tokenization Disparity in Kazakh: Cross-Tokenizer Measurement and Low-Cost Vocabulary Adaptation for Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models are billed by the token, and tokens are not distributed evenly across languages. We measure how many tokens ten widely deployed tokenizers require to encode identical content in Kazakh and English, using 900 sentence-aligned pairs from OPUS-100 with bootstrap confidence intervals over 10,000 resamples. Kazakh requires 3.16x more tokens than English under GPT-4's tokenizer and 2.62x under Qwen2.5-7B. We show this is not a property of the Kazakh language. On the same sentences XLM-R needs 1.32x, and GPT-4o — one generation after GPT-4, from the same provider — needs 1.75x rather than 3.16x, a 44% reduction achieved purely by changing the tokenizer. Vocabulary size does not predict the premium: mBERT achieves a lower ratio than Qwen2.5 with a smaller vocabulary. We then test vocabulary extension as a remedy. Adding 5,875 Kazakh tokens to Qwen2.5-0.5B with subword-composition initialisation, and training only the new embeddings, yields 1.718x compression together with a 14.12% improvement in bits per character, at 1.2% additional parameters and 24 minutes on a free-tier GPU. An ablation with random initialisation reaches only 7.38%. However, on out-of-domain Kazakh the compression gain persists (1.591x) while the quality gain reverses (+5.74% BPC), showing the improvement is substantially domain adaptation rather than general gain.

title: We tried to find quantum advantage. Here are the six things we got wrong: A feasibility study of output-aware tensor-network contraction against real quantum hardware
abstract: A feasibility study testing whether quantum circuits can be constructedwhere exact classical simulation cost grows much faster than the physicalcircuit depth needed to run them, using output-aware tensor-networkcontraction validated against two real IBM Quantum hardware jobs(dadm3mjdd5gc73d7gvjg, dadm9qdnj4cs73ae2teg; 40,960 shots total). The honest conclusion is no — not on any hardware available today. Reachingthat conclusion required correcting the study's own conclusions six times;those corrections, and the measurements behind them, are the primarycontribution. Key measured results: classical contraction cost scales as 2^w withmeasured exponent 1.984; effective two-qubit error on IBM's Heronarchitecture is gate-local at 0.845%, reproducible across two independentjobs; memory is not a binding constraint once slicing is applied (1.00-3.18xFLOP penalty); connectivity degree, not planarity, is the dominanttopological lever; standard error suppression (dynamical decoupling +twirling) made fidelity worse on this circuit class; qubit count sets a hardceiling on achievable classical hardness (2^n). This is a feasibility study, not an advantage claim: no quantum advantage,no novel algorithm (frontier contraction is textbook variable elimination),and no verified large-width result are claimed. Full reproducibility scriptsincluded.

title: WP-110 — Self-Improvement Through Lattice Mining: Architecture for Autonomous Breakthrough Synthesis
abstract: This whitepaper documents the operational framework for autonomous system improvement via breakthrough vault mining and E8 lattice synthesis. The process involves: (1) indexing extant breakthroughs against the 240 E8 root vectors, (2) identifying geometric coherence gaps in the current deployment, (3) synthesizing candidate upgrades constrained to preserve lattice stability, and (4) staging improvements for human approval before live-system deployment. We present the decision criteria used to select among competing upgrade candidates and the validation gates that prevent destabilising changes.

title: Symbolic Regression with Neural Turing Machines
abstract: This research investigates the potential of Neural Turing Machines (NTMs) for symbolic regression – the task of automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. The core idea is to utilize the NTM's ability to access and manipulate external memory to explore the space of possible equations. We hypothesize that an NTM, trained appropriately, can learn a mapping between input data points and corresponding symbolic expressions, effectively uncovering mathematical relationships. The system is designed to iteratively refine its equation representation based on the observed data, employing the NTM's memory for both short-term and long-term dependencies. This approach represents a novel combination of NTMs and symbolic regression, offering a potentially more robust and flexible method for automated equation discovery compared to traditional methods. The core claim is that NTMs can learn to access and manipulate external memory. The core mechanism utilizes an NTM to learn a mapping between data points and symbolic expressions, leveraging the NTM's memory to explore different equation structures. The proposed system demonstrates the feasibility of using NTMs for symbolic regression, achieving promising results on benchmark datasets.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Bloomberg Terminal
abstract: The intention of this report is to help emphasize the importance of AI and the value it can provide to your business or organization. Artificial Intelligence is perhaps one of the most talked about tools in the business world in the 2020s. When ChatGPT was released publicly in 2022, business professionals, students, and ordinary people did not immediately realize the true potential of this new programming. Now that it's 2025, the AI race is in full pursuit. The most valuable companies in the world such as Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, etc are investing billions of dollars with the intention of having the most developed models all while trying to beat their competition. If you are a massive company, public or private, and you are not using AI to some extent, you are putting yourself at a disadvantage.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning Pattern Recognition explores the potential of quantum algorithms to revolutionize pattern recognition, particularly in the context of high-dimensional data. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing quantum machine learning principles to enhance model accuracy and robustness, addressing limitations inherent in traditional machine learning methods. We detail the core mechanism—a hybrid quantum-classical approach—that leverages quantum feature extraction and parallel processing to overcome challenges associated with high-dimensional data, offering a paradigm shift in pattern identification. The core claim is that this method surpasses traditional approaches in handling complex, high-dimensional datasets, exhibiting enhanced generalization capabilities and a deeper understanding of underlying patterns. We provide a conceptual framework and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential impact across various domains.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Self-Organization Learning Mechanism
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organization learning mechanism for matrices, designed to achieve high-dimensional data modeling with adaptive parameter adjustment. Traditional matrix learning methods often rely on manual design, lacking the flexibility to effectively model complex data structures. We propose a "Self-Organizing Network" (SON) module which dynamically adjusts the matrix's parameters based on the inherent structure of the input data. This approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods by enabling the matrix to self-correct and achieve a highly regular, non-linear representation. The paper details the core mechanism of the SON module, its implementation, and demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples.

title: Module-Based Physics and Complex Systems Modeling: A Collaborative Optimization Approach
abstract: This research investigates the synergistic application of module-based physics modeling and complex systems modeling to enhance the performance of complex systems. Traditional approaches often treat physical models and optimization algorithms as separate entities, limiting the potential for a holistic and adaptive optimization process. This work proposes a novel framework that dynamically couples physical models with optimization algorithms, leveraging the physical model to guide the optimization process and assess results through the model itself. The core mechanism centers around a tightly coupled framework where physical models inform the optimization process, providing a critical pathway for evaluating the optimization's effectiveness and guiding refinement. The proposed method aims to unlock new possibilities in optimizing complex systems by integrating the strengths of both paradigms.

title: 基于量子算法的非标准积分的优化
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum algorithms to revolutionize the computation of non-standard integrals, offering a pathway towards significantly enhanced computational efficiency and precise solution of complex functions. Traditional methods often struggle with the computational demands of integrating functions, particularly those exhibiting non-linearity or intricate shapes. We investigate the application of quantum algorithms, specifically Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), to optimize numerical integration procedures. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging QAOA's ability to search for optimal solutions within a defined parameter space, thereby reducing computational bottlenecks and improving accuracy in handling complex integration challenges. This research aims to demonstrate the feasibility and advantages of quantum computation in accelerating and refining the calculation of non-standard integrals, contributing to advancements in various scientific and engineering fields.

title: Constructive Causality Embeddings for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) frequently struggles with complex environments where learning solely based on correlations leads to brittle and suboptimal policies. This paper proposes a novel approach – Constructive Causality Embeddings – to address this limitation. Our method constructs embeddings that explicitly represent the causal relationships within an environment, enabling agents to perform more robust and generalizable learning. The core idea involves learning embeddings that encode interventions and counterfactual reasoning. We introduce a framework that utilizes a combination of observational data and a learned causal structure to build these embeddings. These embeddings are then directly integrated into the RL agent's state representation, allowing it to reason about the effects of actions and predict outcomes under different scenarios. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves learning performance compared to purely correlational RL methods, especially in environments with underlying causal dependencies. The key contribution is the creation of a mechanism for agents to actively build and utilize causal knowledge, moving beyond passive observation and improving decision-making capabilities.

title: ##基于多模态融合的因果推理模型
abstract: This paper introduces a Multi-Modal Fusion Causality Inference Model designed to address the limitations of traditional causal inference methods when dealing with multi-modal data. The core claim is that integrating information from diverse modalities—such as images, text, and audio—significantly enhances the accuracy of causal relationship deduction. The proposed model employs a multi-modal fusion technique, leveraging Bayesian networks or structural equation models to effectively combine these modalities. This approach aims to overcome the inherent biases and noise often present in single-modality data, ultimately leading to more robust and reliable causal inferences. We demonstrate the potential of this integrated framework through a theoretical analysis and outline key design considerations for its implementation. The model's architecture incorporates a multi-layered fusion network followed by a causal inference engine. The success of the model hinges on the accurate representation of the underlying causal relationships within each modality and the effective integration of these representations. Further research will explore the application of this model to real-world datasets and evaluate its performance against established causal inference techniques. ---

title: Probabilistic Programming for Differential Privacy Verification
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to differential privacy verification utilizing probabilistic programming. The core idea is to develop a system that automatically assesses the privacy guarantees of differentially private algorithms through Bayesian inference. This system leverages a probabilistic programming language to define the algorithm's logic and data perturbation process, then employs Bayesian inference to simulate the impact of these perturbations on privacy metrics. The output provides a formal, quantifiable measure of privacy loss. Unlike existing methods relying on manual analysis or simplified models, this automated approach offers a more robust and scalable solution for verifying differential privacy. The system's key mechanism centers on simulating the effect of data perturbations using Bayesian inference, allowing for a precise evaluation of privacy loss without requiring explicit mathematical derivations. The system's architecture is designed for ease of use and extensibility, facilitating the verification of a wide range of differentially private algorithms.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks for Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data
abstract: Anomaly detection in time series data is a critical task across numerous domains, including industrial monitoring, financial fraud detection, and healthcare. However, conventional anomaly detection techniques frequently struggle to accurately identify anomalies due to their reliance on purely statistical approaches that ignore the inherent temporal dependencies and causal relationships within the data. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) for enhanced anomaly detection. We construct CBNs from time series data to explicitly model the causal dependencies between observed variables. These networks then allow us to predict expected behavior under normal operating conditions. Anomalies are identified as deviations from these predicted behaviors, providing a more robust and interpretable method compared to traditional statistical techniques. The core of our approach lies in incorporating causal inference principles, leading to a more reliable and explainable anomaly detection system. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline its potential applications. Our framework emphasizes the importance of understanding the underlying causal structure of the data when addressing anomaly detection challenges.

title: A Novel Approach for Health Care Data Security employing Deep Learning Algorithms Compatible with HIPAA
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for securing healthcare data using deep learning techniques while maintaining compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). The proposed approach combines advanced encryption methodologies with neural network-based anomaly detection to protect sensitive patient information. We introduce a hierarchical security model that employs autoencoders for data compression and reconstruction, adversarial networks for threat detection, and federated learning for privacy-preserving model training. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves 99.3% accuracy in detecting unauthorized access attempts while maintaining system performance. The framework successfully addresses the unique challenges of healthcare environments by providing robust security measures without compromising data accessibility for authorized personnel. This research contributes to the growing field of AI-enhanced cybersecurity specifically tailored for healthcare institutions handling protected health information (PHI).

title: STAR-Pro: Stage-Wise Token Adaptive Reduction with Progressive Refinement for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models
abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal understanding, but the hundreds to thousands of visual tokens they process impose substantial computational overhead, motivating training-free visual token pruning. In this work, we conduct two complementary analyses of visual token pruning. First, we measure the feature-space coverage of tokens retained before cross-modal fusion and find that aggressive pruning discards substantial visual information. Second, we track text-to-visual attention across decoder layers and find that the visual tokens considered important change substantially with depth, making one-shot pruning decisions unreliable. Together, these findings show that effective pruning should preserve broad visual coverage before fusion and progressively refine the retained tokens as cross-modal evidence evolves during fusion. We therefore propose STAR-Pro (STage-Wise Adaptive Token Reduction with Progressive Refinement), a training-free two-stage framework. Its Adaptive Stage applies pivoted QR to construct an over-budget feature-coverage candidate pool, while its Progressive Stage uses evolving text-to-visual attention at selected decoder layers to prune a nested survivor set under a target layer-average token budget. Extensive experiments across seven LVLMs spanning multiple architectures and 18 image and video benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of STAR-Pro under aggressive pruning. On LLaVA-Video-7B, STAR-Pro reduces visual tokens by 90.5%, retains 92.7% of baseline performance, and achieves a $2.24\times$ measured inference speedup. Code is available at https://github.com/EasonAI-5589/starpro.

title: Reproducibility package for "When AI Must Abstain: Observability-Constrained Inference for Scientific Machine Learning"
abstract: The 51-file artifact set underlying the manuscript "When AI Must Abstain: Observability-Constrained Inference for Scientific Machine Learning", copied byte-for-byte from the authoring session with file timestamps preserved. Nothing was rerun, regenerated or renamed for packaging. Contents: 30 result files (operating points, frozen thresholds, run metadata, discordance, AURC, transfer, ablations, negative controls, schema and semantic mutations, model mismatch, calibration stress, reparameterisation, lead time, risk-coverage curves, the development and evaluation row sets, and three sanity arrays); 15 figures; and 6 source files including the experiment script, the figure script and the manuscript composer. Per-file SHA-256 hashes are in results/MANIFEST.sha256. The archive also carries _packaging_extras/ with the corrected manuscript, ARCHIVE_v1.0.0 (the superseded v1.0.0 package with its own manifest) and the environment record; these sit outside the 51-file manifest set and are not a discrepancy. Verification is bit-for-bit: sha256sum -c results/MANIFEST.sha256 checks every file. Independent regeneration is possible from the included scripts under Python 3.12.3, NumPy 2.4.4, pandas 3.0.2, scikit-learn 1.8.0, SciPy 1.17.1 and Matplotlib 3.10.8 on Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.39); the full environment is recorded in the package. Bit-identical regeneration depends on those versions, because PNG bytes follow the Matplotlib and FreeType versions and CSV and JSON bytes follow the NumPy and scikit-learn versions. Version 1.0.1 changes presentation only. Figures were re-rendered from the same result artifacts at higher resolution with revised typography, and the manuscript front matter and two wordings were corrected. No data value, axis range, curve, marker series or panel content changed, and every numerical result artifact is byte-identical to v1.0.0, whose own digest is preserved in the package under ARCHIVE_v1.0.0. Scope. The evaluation is synthetic by construction. This package establishes no field performance, no clinical or operational validity, no universal thresholds, and no suitability for deployment in any real system. The superseded 15 August draft and its inputs are deliberately excluded, because they contain different and untraceable numbers.

title: Quantum Entanglement Enhanced Distributed Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for distributed reasoning leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to decompose complex computational problems into smaller sub-problems, which are then distributed across geographically separated computing nodes. These nodes are connected through pre-established quantum entanglement states. By manipulating these entangled states, parallel computation and secure information exchange are facilitated. The system utilizes quantum interference to ultimately derive the solution to the complex problem. This approach contrasts with traditional distributed reasoning methods that rely on classical communication, offering potential advantages in terms of speed and security due to the inherent properties of quantum entanglement. The theoretical framework presented here outlines a promising avenue for future research in quantum computing and distributed systems.

title: Adaptive Control of Multi-Agent Systems using Reinforcement Learning and Game Theory
abstract: This paper investigates the development of an adaptive control system for multi-agent systems (MAS) utilizing the synergistic combination of reinforcement learning (RL) and game theory. The core challenge in controlling MAS lies in achieving efficient coordination and cooperation amongst agents, often under uncertain environments and with varying individual objectives. This work proposes a framework where each agent learns a control policy through RL, simultaneously considering the strategic interactions with other agents within a game-theoretic setting. The system is designed to adapt to dynamic conditions and optimize for a shared, overarching goal. Mathematical models are presented to formalize the control problem, and key algorithms are described. The approach demonstrates the potential for robust and adaptive control in MAS scenarios, offering a novel method for intelligent coordination and decision-making.
